transcript:
Header: 2026-09-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Evelyn (Vanguardix ML Eng), Carlos (Head of AI), Priya (Infra), Liam (Product)

Summary (auto): quick recap of last week's benchmarks, decision to test pinning strategy, discuss rollback/fallback approach and security checklist.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll kick off, quick roll call?
[00:08] Evelyn: Evelyn here.
[00:10] Carlos: Carlos.
[00:12] Priya: Priya here.
[00:15] Liam: Liam.
[00:17] Marcus: Marcus from Redwood.
[00:20] Sofia: Cool. Agenda: results review, pinning proposal, fallback/rollback plan, next steps. Marcus, do you want to lead the perf notes?
[00:30] Marcus: Yep. So we re-ran the suite you sent last week against the catalog variants. The main delta is tail latency on the 8k prompts and hallucination frequency for the financial QAs. On hosted v2.1.3-quant we see median token latency ~12ms/token and p95 ~45ms/token, cost per 1k tokens about $3.10. On v2.0.9 (non-quant) median is 14ms/token p95 70ms/token cost ~$3.40. There's also a tiny uptick in hallucinations on v2.1.3 with the aggressive sampling we used, about 2.7% vs 1.8% on 2.0.9.
[01:20] Evelyn: Okay interesting. The hallucination number is a bit concerning — those are the ones that hallucinate account balances or trajectories, right?
[01:28] Marcus: Yeah that's the set that hallucinated factuals. But if we apply the prompt templates you shared with stricter system instructions it drops to about 1.6% on the v2.1.3 quant. So the prompt layer matters.
[01:40] Carlos: So is the plan to pin v2.1.3 for latency, but use v2.0.9 as a fallback? How transparent is that to our app?
[01:49] Sofia: Exactly, we recommend pinning the pilot route to v2.1.3-quant for the bulk of traffic and configure an automatic fallback to v2.0.9 if latency or error thresholds are breached. Marcus can explain routing.
[02:05] Marcus: Yep — Redwood routing supports policy-based fallbacks. You can set SLOs at token p95 or error rate. If breached for more than X seconds or Y requests, traffic shifts automatically to the fallback model. We'll also keep a canary with 1% to detect regressions.
[02:22] Priya: Quick infra question — for the dedicated pilot we plan to put Redwood Dedicated inside our VPC with peering. Will the pinned model still be manageable from the console? We need to ensure KMS/HSM keys remain under our control.
[02:33] Sofia: Yes, for Private / Dedicated we offer customer-managed KMS integration and audit logs. You'll still be able to pin via the control plane; the control plane communicates with the private runtime using your certs. We'll include the detailed security pack.
[02:47] Liam: Can we see a quick example of the rollback policy and what triggers it?
[02:52] Marcus: Sure. Example: policy that checks p95 latency > 120ms for 30s OR hallucination/error rate > 3% over a 5m window. If triggered, traffic moves to fallback model immediate, we notify and create automatic rollback ticket. You can tune thresholds.
[03:12] Evelyn: When you say hallucination/error rate detection, is that based on our eval set or live heuristics?
[03:18] Marcus: Both — we support live heuristic detectors (e.g., contradiction detection, hallucination classifiers) and you can also ship an eval set for batched checks. For POC we recommend using your 50 failing prompts we discussed plus live metrics.
[03:34] Priya: About quantization: we have compliance questions — is quantized model run in a way that affects output determinism? We need to ensure results are stable for audits.
[03:43] Marcus: Quantization can introduce small numeric differences but we haven't seen systematic output drift that would break correctness for retrieval-augmented financial tasks. For audits we can freeze a pinned binary image and keep model checksums in the audit log.
[03:58] Carlos: That's helpful. Also, about cost — the numbers you quoted are hosted; how different would dedicated be?
[04:05] Marcus: Dedicated pricing depends on reserved capacity and instance mix. For example, a small dedicated pool optimized for v2.1.3 quant runs about 30-40% cheaper per token at scale because of throughput gains and continuous batching. Sofia will follow up with pricing options.
[04:21] Sofia: I'll send a dedicated pilot pricing sheet and a few commitment tiers after the call.
[04:25] Liam: On pinning — can we route based on customer tier? e.g., premium customers on pinned v2.1.3, others on cheaper fallback?
[04:33] Marcus: Yes, routing rules can be header-based (customer tier), region, or token budget. We can show examples in the console.
[04:40] Evelyn: One data point — last week our bench saw a few outlier prompts that took >300ms p99 on 8k context. Were those reproduced in your runs?
[04:50] Marcus: We saw similar p99 outliers, tied to long attention windows with many retrieved docs. We suggest prefix caching (KV cache) on repeated prefixes; it reduced those outliers by ~40% in our internal tests.
[05:05] Priya: Does KV cache persist across restarts? We need to understand cache invalidation and TTLs for GDPR concerns.
[05:12] Marcus: Cache TTLs are configurable; for Private you control retention and invalidation. We'll include docs about cache lifecycle and compliance controls.
[05:20] Carlos: On fallback testing — can we simulate a rollback in staging? We want to see end-to-end behavior including telemetry and customer-facing errors.
[05:28] Marcus: Absolutely. We can run a controlled failover on your staging route so you can validate alerting, SLO triggers, and SDK behavior.
[05:34] Evelyn: Regarding hallucinations — I want to be clear on evaluation: the 50 failing prompts will be our ground truth and we also want automated regression alerts tied to the eval set, right?
[05:44] Marcus: Yes. Redwood Optimize can monitor a pinned eval set and alert on regressions; you can set sensitivity and who gets notified.
[05:53] Sofia: Quick logistics: Evelyn, you said you'd share the failing Prompts. Can you confirm timeline?
[05:58] Evelyn: I can get those by end of Thursday, 24th.
[06:02] Sofia: Great. Marcus, any bench runs to schedule?
[06:05] Marcus: I'd like to run the dedicated 8k context bench on 28th; need Priya to confirm VPC windows.
[06:12] Priya: I can confirm peering window on the 27th; 28th is fine for bench.
[06:16] Liam: A question on RBAC — can we limit who can change pinning rules? We don't want product to accidentally flip pilot config.
[06:22] Marcus: Yes RBAC + audit logs. You can set role that only ops or security can change rollout policies. All changes are logged with diffs.
[06:30] Carlos: Any known incompatibilities between v2.1.3-quant and our current retrieval? e.g., tokenization differences?
[06:36] Marcus: No major tokenization differences; we did note a subtle delimiter handling change in 2.1.2 which we fixed in 2.1.3. We'll share a short note on tokenization.
[06:46] Evelyn: One more ask — can you provide a quick script to SR the canary behavior and collect traces so we can feed into our observability?
[06:53] Marcus: Yes we'll provide a script that hits the canary route with synthetic traffic and exports traces to your tracing endpoint.
[07:00] Sofia: Ok let's recap and assign action items.
[07:05] Marcus: I'll run latency/cost matrix for pinned v2.1.3 vs 2.0.9 and include p50/p95/p99 and cost lines, deliver by 2026-09-29.
[07:15] Evelyn: I'll share the 50 failing prompts and expected outputs by 2026-09-24.
[07:20] Sofia: I'll send pricing and security docs by 2026-09-24 and coordinate the bench run on 2026-09-28.
[07:27] Priya: I'll confirm VPC peering window by 2026-09-25.
[07:33] Liam: We'll validate rollback in staging during the bench run.
[07:38] Carlos: Sounds good. Also curious about long-term: if we move to production, what does canary % look like for safe rollouts?
[07:44] Marcus: Typical path: 1% canary for 30m, then 5% for 1-2 hours, then 25% for a day, then full. But you can tighten based on customer risk profile.
[07:57] Evelyn: Thanks all. One minor note: there was a transcription mismatch in last week's notes where our internal model name got swapped; we'll reconcile names in the prompt doc.
[08:05] Sofia: Good catch. We'll also make sure versions are explicit.
[08:10] Sofia: Any final questions?
[08:12] Carlos: None from me. Thanks.
[08:14] Priya: All good.
[08:16] Marcus: Thanks, we'll follow up with the matrix and scripts.
[08:20] Sofia: Great — we'll send a short email with the next steps.
